about: A byte string crosses a <param> and a <donedata> as its byte-exact Latin-1 text, each byte the character of that code point. The host raises framed.taken with some bytes, the machine keeps them in `held`, sends them to itself as the <param>s of framed.relayed and reads that event back into `echo`, so what arrived is what was held; the final's <donedata> carries `echo` the same way. A byte above 0x7F is the character of its code point on the wire, and a quote, a backslash and a control byte are the escapes a JSON string needs for them. Expected values are derived from the bytes, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: nothing has been held or relayed yet
the host raises bytes above 0x7F: the machine keeps them
they cross as the <param> of a message to itself and are read back as the bytes that were held
no bytes at all is a byte string of length zero, and crosses as the empty text
the empty byte string arrives as the empty byte string
the bytes a JSON string escapes: a quote, a backslash, a newline, the control byte 0x01, an accented letter, 'z' and '!' fill the eight
all eight arrive as they were
the final's <donedata> carries `echo` as the same text
